sample_unit: questions (each presented twice to four ChatGPT versions)

links.outcome: Accuracy, completeness, and guideline consistency of ChatGPT answers on fecal incontinence
links.effect: No version was entirely accurate, complete, or guideline-consistent; accuracy 61% (3.5), 72% (4), 50% (5 Free), 83% (5 Plus); most frequent error theme was inaccurate treatment recommendations.
links.quote: No version of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer provided answers that were entirely accurate, complete, or consistent with clinical practice guidelines; however, the paid version performed markedly better than the other versions.

links.outcome: Clinical answer quality of general-purpose chatbot versions against society guidelines
links.effect: General-purpose ChatGPT versions failed to give fully accurate/complete/guideline-consistent answers; accuracy ranged 50% to 83%, with GPT-5 Free lowest on accuracy at 50%.
links.quote: Reviewers rated 61% of answers accurate, 65% complete, and 68% consistent for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-3.5; 72%, 73%, and 69% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-4; 50%, 73%, 68% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 Free; and 83%, 95%, and 82% for Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 Plus, respectively.

links.outcome: Difference in answer quality between free and paid ChatGPT-5 versions
links.effect: Paywall-contingent performance: GPT-5 Plus accuracy 83% vs GPT-5 Free 50%; completeness 95% vs 73%.
links.quote: Analysis of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 Free versus Plus highlighted a dimension of disparity introduced by paywall-contingent model performance.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy, completeness, and guideline consistency of ChatGPT responses to lay questions about fecal incontinence without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
